items.q: How much does it cost to study medicine (MBBS) in Ukraine?
items.a: The only reliable figure is the university's own fee schedule for your programme and intake. When you read it, check the academic year, the currency, and whether the fee is per year, per semester or for the whole programme. Ask what it includes, for example a preparatory course, accommodation, insurance or a medical examination. Fees for different years, currencies or programmes cannot be compared directly. Our [tuition fees guide](/tuition-fees/) shows how to read a fee schedule. We show a university's fee only after reading it on that schedule, with the date we checked it.

items.q: How many years does medicine (MBBS) take in Ukraine?
items.a: Check the length on the university's own programme page for your intake; we do not give a general figure. Look at the number of years of study, whether a preparatory year or an internship is counted separately, and the exact title of the qualification. “MBBS” is how many applicants search, but each university awards its own qualification title. We show a programme's length on a university's profile only after reading it there. See also [medicine (MBBS) in Ukraine](/courses/medicine/).

items.q: Do I need biology and chemistry to apply?
items.a: It depends on the university, the programme, your school-leaving qualification and the intake, so there is no universal answer. On the university's programme page or admission rules, check which subjects it asks for, the minimum grades and the grading scale it uses, and whether there is an entrance test or interview. The [admissions guide](/admissions/#readiness) lists the checks to make, and you can ask us about a specific programme in your candidate profile.

items.q: Is NEET required to study MBBS in Ukraine?
items.a: If you plan to practise in India, check two things before you apply. First, read the current rules of India's National Medical Commission (NMC) on its own website, including anything they say about NEET: the NMC, not a Ukrainian university or an agent, decides what it requires of doctors who studied abroad. Second, ask the university whether it asks for a NEET result in its own admission requirements, and keep its answer in writing. We do not summarise the NMC's rules here.

items.q: Is an MBBS from Ukraine valid in India?
items.a: In India, the National Medical Commission (NMC) sets the rules that doctors who studied abroad must meet before they can register to practise; no university, agent or website, including this one, decides that. Read the NMC's current rules on its own website before you apply, check your chosen programme against them, and keep a note of what you read and when. If anything is unclear, ask the NMC. We do not publish recognition claims.

items.q: Is a Ukrainian medical degree accepted in Germany, Canada or other countries?
items.a: That is decided by the regulator for your profession in the country where you plan to work, not by the university, an agent or us. Find that regulator's own website, read what it currently asks of doctors who qualified abroad, and check your chosen programme against it before you apply. We do not publish recognition claims for any country.
